publication.title: Gaze-in-wild: A dataset for studying eye and head coordination in everyday activities

status_legend.multiple_labellers: recording has labels from multiple labellers
status_legend.single_labeller: recording is labeled by a single person

metadata_discrepancy.interpretation: The disagreement is preserved as unresolved metadata provenance and is not repaired or used to infer participant identity.

claim_limits: The 19 person numbers are a publication-level supplementary-table identity set, not yet a file-by-file distributed-data participant mapping.
The four named task columns are verified from Supplementary Table 1, but the complete TrIdx-to-task mapping is not frozen from this evidence.
The ParticipantInfo age discrepancy for participant 18 is preserved and prevents using age metadata as an identity join.
No exact compressed dataset copy, dataset-file rights, timestamp cadence, labeller-stream recoverability, agreement, model performance, cross-dataset performance, or GP3 validity is established.
next_required_actions: Obtain and fingerprint the exact authoritative compressed Gaze-in-the-Wild dataset copy.
Verify dataset-file analysis-use and redistribution terms independently of article and repository-software licenses.
Bind the published 19-person table numbers to exact distributed participant/file identities without relying on age metadata.
Verify the complete TrIdx-to-task mapping against authoritative data or source documentation.
Freeze the per-person task/labelling-status matrix only from an exact reviewed supplementary source copy if needed for downstream sensitivity analyses.
